 \end{description}
 
+\subsection{The type of \KWD{self} in a trait with a self-type parameter}
+\seclabel{revival-self-type}
+
+\begin{description}
+\item[Affected sections] \secref{idn-ref}; \secref{trait-decls}; \secref{methods}.
+\item[Change] In \secref{idn-ref}, a sentence after the one on the self-type
+idiom: in a declaration of a trait \VAR{T} with no \KWD{comprises} clause and a
+self-type parameter \VAR{X}, \KWD{self} has the type \EXP{T \cap X} in the bodies of
+the trait's methods, and the \KWD{self} parameter keeps the type \VAR{T} in the
+signature of each method declaration.
+In \secref{trait-decls}, a paragraph after the one on \KWD{comprises} clauses
+defines a self-type parameter: a static parameter of a trait with no
+\KWD{comprises} clause that is bounded by the trait at its own static
+parameters, or by an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter that the
+trait also lists in its \KWD{extends} clause, with that static parameter as the
+static argument for the self-type parameter.
+The paragraph requires every trait or object declaration and every object
+expression that extends an instantiation of such a trait to be a subtype of
+the static argument of that instantiation for the self-type parameter, a trait with
+a self-type parameter of its own standing as the intersection of its type and that
+parameter, and gives an example marked ``Not allowed''.
+In \secref{methods}, a box after the sentence that a functional method's
+\KWD{self} parameter implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object
+says that the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature.
+Each of the three passages has a box.
+\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A; it follows the
+revival's decision of 13~October 2026 on the bodies of the self-typed traits,
+and its second form of a self-type parameter, through a trait that the trait
+extends, follows a default taken under that decision on 14~October 2026.
+\library\ declare their orders and their algebra as traits whose static
+parameter is bounded by the trait itself, as in
+\EXP{\KWD{trait}\;\TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I \KWD{extends} \TYP{Integral}\llbracket{}I\rrbracket\rrbracket},
+and give them default bodies that return \KWD{self} where that parameter is
+declared, or pass it where the parameter is expected: the team's minimal
+complete definitions, such as \OPR{MIN} on \TYP{StandardTotalOrder} and
+\VAR{floor} on \TYP{Integral}.
+The interpreter runs them; the compiled type checker refused 29 of them,
+since it typed \KWD{self} as the trait.
+A bound constrains the static argument, not \KWD{self}: an object may extend
+\EXP{\TYP{Integral}\llbracket\mathbb{Z}32\rrbracket} without being a
+\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and a body that treats \KWD{self} as the parameter is sound
+only if every declaration that extends the trait is a subtype of its static
+argument for that parameter.
+Scala states that rule for its declared self types (``The self type of a class
+or object must conform to the self types of all classes which are inherited by
+the template'', \emph{Scala Language Specification 2.13}, section 5.1); the revival reads the self type from the bound, which \library\
+already write, as the team's compiled type checker reads it from a
+\KWD{comprises} clause (\secref{idn-ref}), a reading that the team's gated test
+\nolinkurl{ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXX10k.test} pins.
+Naden's account of the Return Type Rule (2012) asked that the self-type idiom
+become ``a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but
+instead only in bounds''
+(\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex}, lines 626--630).
+The signatures keep the type of the trait because the type group's account of
+overloading of 2019 (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu, POPL 2019) assumes, for the
+completeness of its matching of types, that no declared type holds a type
+parameter inside an intersection (pp.~11:21--22), and its Return Type Rule
+compares declared domains (p.~11:13): with the intersection in the signatures,
+the domains of the two declarations of \OPR{CMP} on \TYP{StandardPartialOrder}
+and \TYP{StandardTotalOrder} became equivalent, and the compiled type checker
+reported 18 errors of the Return Type Rule that the declarations do not make.
+The second form of a self-type parameter keeps valid as written the mixins of
+\library\ that the team wrote in 2009, \TYP{ContainmentBySubset} and
+\TYP{ContainmentByComparison}, whose static parameter is bounded by the trait
+\TYP{Containment}, which they extend at it.
+The full reasoning is in
+\nolinkurl{explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md} and
+\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-self-type/decision-record.md} in the
+revival's repository.
+\item[Effect] The compiled type checker types \KWD{self} as \EXP{T \cap X} in
+the bodies of the dotted and functional methods of a trait with a self
+parameter \VAR{X}, keeps \VAR{T} in the signatures that overloading, the Return
+Type Rule and the choice of a declaration at a call read, and refuses a trait
+or object declaration or an object expression that the new paragraph of
+\secref{trait-decls} does not allow, with the message
+``\VAR{D} extends \EXP{C\llbracket{}A\rrbracket}, whose self parameter is \VAR{A},
+but \VAR{D} is not a subtype of \VAR{A}.''.

+declaration that the paragraph refuses.
+The code generator compiles a default body that returns \KWD{self} as the self
+parameter with no conversion to the type of the instance, so a program that
+runs such a body, which the compiled type checker now accepts, fails the JVM's
+verification when the body's class is loaded (row~695 of the revival's gap
+ledger).
+\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex},
+lines 53--54 and 64--69, which stand unchanged and are now followed by the new
+sentence:
+\begin{quote}
+The type of \KWD{self} is the type of the trait or object being declared by
+the innermost enclosing trait or object declaration or object expression.
+\end{quote}
+and
+\begin{quote}
+If the innermost enclosing such construct is a trait declaration (for a trait
+called, say, `\EXP{T}'), and that trait declaration has a \KWD{comprises}
+clause, and `\EXP{U_1}', `\EXP{U_2}', ..., `\EXP{U_n}' are the traits mentioned
+in the \KWD{comprises} clause, then the type of \KWD{self} is instead
+``\EXP{T \cap (U_{\mathrm{1}} \cup U_{\mathrm{2}} \cup \ldots \cup U_{\mathrm{n}})}''.
+\end{quote}
+The paragraph of \secref{trait-decls} is new.
+\nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex}, line 486, the end of the
+sentence of \secref{methods} that the new box follows, stands unchanged:
+\begin{quote}
+and implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object.
+\end{quote}
+\item[Route C] Under route~C a self-typed trait is read by a \KWD{comprises}
+clause that lists its static parameter, as the compiled path's own library
+declares its orders (\nolinkurl{Library/CompilerAlgebra.fsi}, lines 16 and 24,
+in the revival's repository); under such a clause the self-type idiom of
+\secref{idn-ref} types \KWD{self}, and this rule is not reached.
+A return to that form would need the clause on the self-typed traits of
+\library, which would also close each of them to its static parameter; a way
+for the interpreter past its stack overflow on a clause that lists a static
+parameter (row~407 of the revival's gap ledger); and leave in
+\secref{trait-decls} for a static parameter as a listed type, which the type
+group's calculus of 2012 does not admit.
+\end{description}

set -euo pipefail
USAGE='usage: old-fortress.sh <base-build> <private-caches> <fortress arguments>...'
BASE=$(realpath "${1:?$USAGE}")
PRIV_ARG=${2:?$USAGE}
shift 2
[ -x "$BASE/bin/fortress" ] && [ -e "$BASE/ProjectFortress/build/com/sun/fortress/Shell.class" ] \
  && [ -e "$BASE/default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar" ] \
  || { echo "old-fortress: $BASE is not a built tree" >&2 ; exit 2 ; }
PRIV=$(realpath -m "$PRIV_ARG")
case "$PRIV/" in "$BASE"/*) echo "old-fortress: $PRIV is inside the base build $BASE" >&2 ; exit 2 ;; esac
if [ ! -d "$PRIV" ]; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$PRIV")"
    PART="$PRIV.part.$$"
    cp -a "$BASE/default_repository/caches" "$PART"
    mv -T "$PART" "$PRIV" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "$PART"     # another run made it first: use that one
fi
FORTRESS_HOME="$BASE" FORTRESS_CACHES="$PRIV" exec "$BASE/bin/fortress" "$@"

# Decision record: the type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter (rung S, climb batch 14)

This is the decision record the S1 form asks for (POSITIONS, "The S1 form"; the `fortress-repo` skill's `references/specification.md`, "Changing the text: the revision form", part 4): each changed passage, the original and the new text, the reason, and the way back. Appendix I's entry "The type of `self` in a trait with a self-type parameter" (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3296-3412`, `\seclabel{revival-self-type}`) names this file. The base is `5bf8a7c84`. "The Working Draft of February 2011" is the unrevised copy under `Specification-1.0-frozen/`.

The decision this rung carries out is P-146, "The checker reads `self` in a self-typed trait's method bodies as the implementing type (way 6)", from the judgement's recommendation (`explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, section 4), with the default the coordinator took under it after the batch record's review and listed for review (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`): a trait's type parameter bounded by a self-typed trait that the trait extends at that parameter counts as the trait's self parameter too, never an object's. The form follows P-95 and P-96.

## 1. A word, before the passages

The specification already says "self parameter" for the parameter named `self` of a method (`Specification/basic/overloading.tex:167-182`, `Specification/basic/traits.tex:577`, `:591`, `:631`, `:644`, `Specification/preliminaries/overview.tex:1140-1146`). The checker's code and the record call the trait's static parameter that `self` is read as "the self parameter" (`SelfParamDisambiguator.selfParam`; the judgement, way 6). So the text calls the static parameter a **self-type parameter**, and keeps "self parameter" for `self`. The checker's message keeps the record's wording, "whose self parameter is A" (the batch record, section S, "Rule (b), not yet built"), which reads as the instantiation's argument for the trait's static self parameter.

## 2. The passages

### 2.1 The type of `self` (`Specification/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex`, section "Identifier References")

- Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/expressions/var-ref.tex:53-54` and `:64-69`, the same text as the base's `var-ref.tex:53-54`, `:64-69`, unchanged by this rung: "The type of `self` is the type of the trait or object being declared by the innermost enclosing trait or object declaration or object expression." and the self-type idiom, "If the innermost enclosing such construct is a trait declaration (for a trait called, say, `T`), and that trait declaration has a `comprises` clause, and `U_1`, `U_2`, ..., `U_n` are the traits mentioned in the `comprises` clause, then the type of `self` is instead `T ∩ (U_1 ∪ U_2 ∪ ... ∪ U_n)`."
- New text, `var-ref.tex:70-79`, after the idiom's sentence: "If that trait declaration has no `comprises` clause and has a self-type parameter `X` (§ trait-decls), a static parameter bounded by the trait itself at its own static parameters, as in `trait T[\X extends T[\X\]\]`, or by a trait with a self-type parameter that `T` extends at `X`, then the type of `self` in the bodies of its methods is instead `T ∩ X`; the `self` parameter keeps the type `T` in the signature of each method declaration, which overloading and the choice of a declaration at a call read." The callout follows at `:80-90`.
- Reason. Rule (a) of way 6 (the judgement, section 3, "Way 6"): a bound constrains the argument, not `self`; a body that treats `self` as the parameter is sound only under a further fact, which Scala gets from a declared self type checked at each extender. The checker's own self type under a `comprises` clause (`SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:56-75`, `TypeAnalyzer.removeSelf`), which the team pinned in `XXX10k.test`, is read from the bound that the library already writes. Naden asked for exactly this, "a separate construct which cannot be used as a first class type, but instead only in bounds" (`Papers/Types/journal/justificationOfRTR.tex:626-630`).
- The confinement's reason, the signatures kept at the trait's type. The POPL 2019 paper (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu) has no self types, so it neither supports nor contradicts rules (a) and (b); but its matching of types is complete only for types that hold no type parameter inside a union or intersection, an assumption it shows every declared type meets (pp. 11:21-22, `research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md:258-264`), and its Return Type Rule compares declared domains (p. 11:13). The unconfined rule put `C[\X\] & X` into the functional methods' signatures and the distance stage then reported 18 Return Type Rule errors between `StandardPartialOrder`'s and `StandardTotalOrder`'s `CMP`, whose domains became equivalent, and 3 call sites typed `Comparison` (the judgement, "Rule (a) alone, as section 6 asks"; `explorations/reviews/array-judgements-popl-check.md`, section 5). Keeping the self parameter at the plain trait type in `FunctionalMethod`'s signature keeps every declared type within the paper's assumption; a later widening of the self type into signatures leaves the paper's ground.

### 2.2 Self-type parameters and their extenders (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, section "Trait Declarations")

- Original: none; the paragraph is new, at `traits.tex:285-326`, after the `comprises` passage and its note on `...` (`:235-283`) and before the `Catalyst` example.
- New text: a trait with no `comprises` clause may have a self-type parameter, a static parameter `X` whose bounds include the trait at its own static parameters, or an instantiation of a trait with a self-type parameter that the trait also lists in its `extends` clause, with `X` as the static argument for that self-type parameter; `self` then has the type `T ∩ X` in its methods' bodies; a trait or object declaration, or an object expression, that extends an instantiation of `T` must be a subtype of the static argument for the self-type parameter, a trait with its own self-type parameter `Y` standing as the intersection of its type and `Y`; an object declaration has none. The example, `trait Shape[\S extends Shape[\S\]\] end`, `object Point extends Shape[\Point\] end`, and `object Mark extends Shape[\Point\] end` marked "Not allowed" in the chapter's form (as at `traits.tex:355-359` and `:372-376`). The callout follows at `:317-326`.
- Reason. Rule (b) of way 6: Scala's conformance rule, "The self type of a class or object must conform to the self types of all classes which are inherited by the template" (*Scala Language Specification 2.13*, section 5.1, as `explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-ways.md:304` cites it). Checking direct extensions at every declaration suffices, by induction up the hierarchy: a value of `C[\A\]` comes from an object whose every supertrait was checked (the judgement, way 6, (b)). The widened reading (the coordinator's default) keeps the team's 2009 mixins `ContainmentBySubset[\T extends Containment[\T\]\] extends Containment[\T\]` and `ContainmentByComparison` (`Library/Containment.fsi:22-30`, `.fss:42`, `:57`) valid as written, rule (b) then checking their extenders, `Relation` among them (`Library/Relation.fsi:17`, `.fss:23`). An object has no self-type parameter, so `object M[\T extends Shape[\T\]\] extends Shape[\T\]` is refused: the object is where rule (b) closes the check that a trait passes down.

### 2.3 The type of a functional method's `self` parameter (`Specification/basic/traits.tex`, section "Method Declarations")

- Original: `Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/traits.tex:486`, unchanged at `traits.tex:598`: "This parameter is not given a type and implicitly has the type of the enclosing trait or object."
- New text: a callout at `traits.tex:599-603`: under a self-type parameter the sentence still holds of the declaration's signature, and in the body `self` has the type `T ∩ X`. The sentence stays true under the confinement, so it is not revised; the callout says so. `Specification/basic/overloading.tex:180-182`, "Note that the static type of the self parameter is the trait or object trait type in which the declaration occurs", stays true for the same reason and gets no callout.

### 2.4 Appendix I

One entry before "Passages not yet revised", `changes.tex:3296-3412`: affected sections, change, rationale (P-146 by its date, 13 October 2026, and the default by its date, 14 October 2026; the library's 29 bodies; Scala's rule; the team's `XXX10k`; Naden; the 2019 paper's reason for the confinement), effect (the checker; walk unchanged and loading what the rule refuses; the code generator's `VerifyError`, row 695), the original text of `var-ref.tex` quoted and `traits.tex:486` named, and route C.

The calculi of Appendix A are untouched, with no new callout: they type `self` as the trait and admit no self type, which their existing callouts already say they predate (the judgement, section 5, "Specification").

## 3. The way back

- To P-146's letter, without the default: the widened reading goes (the second form of a self-type parameter, in `SelfParamDisambiguator.throughBound` and its environment, and the text's "or by a trait with a self-type parameter that `T` extends at `X`"), and rule (b) then refuses the two `Containment` mixins' extension of `Containment[\T\]` until their text changes. `SelfTypeMixinBound` turns red, `XXXSelfTypeMixinExtenderWrong` red ("Saw wrong failure").
- To the Working Draft: rule (a), the confinement and rule (b) go; the 29 library bodies are refused again by the checker (the distance's S1 and R4 classes, 29 sites).
- To route C or way 5, the team's clause: the self-typed traits of the library carry `comprises X`, under which the idiom of `var-ref.tex:64-69` types `self` and rule (a) is not reached; that needs the clause on the seven traits, walk's row 407 repaired first, and leave in `traits.tex` for a static parameter as a listed type, which Welterweight's grammar does not admit (the judgement, section 3, "Way 5"). The entry's Route C item says so.

## 4. What it bends

The record's reading of route A, "no self type enters the library" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-8.md:113`), is set aside by P-146 itself: the library's text gains no self type and no clause, but the checker gives `self` a self type in every trait with a self-type parameter, the library's among them. Route A (P-43) and the `comprises` decision (P-44) stand: under a `comprises` clause the self type is the clause's, and rule (a) is never reached there.

content.content:
If a trait declaration of \VAR{T} includes a \KWD{comprises} clause
then every type listed in its \KWD{comprises} clause extends \VAR{T},
and every value of type \VAR{T} is a value of one of the listed types.
A listed type may be an instantiation of a parameterized trait,
provided that every static variable that occurs in its static arguments
is a static parameter of \VAR{T}
or a \KWD{where}-clause variable of the declaration of \VAR{T}
(\secref{where-clauses}),
which the listed type then holds at every value of:
a trait declared
\EXP{\KWD{trait}\;\TYP{NatParam}\;\KWD{comprises}\;\{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket\}\;\KWD{where}\;\llbracket\KWD{nat}\;n\rrbracket}
lists \EXP{N\llbracket{}n\rrbracket} at every \KWD{nat} value of \VAR{n}.
A trait or object that explicitly extends \VAR{T}
must be a subtype of a listed type,
unless it is a trait with a \KWD{comprises} clause of its own
each of whose listed types meets this requirement,
or a trait with static parameters
such that at least one trait or object extends it
and every trait or object that extends it
is a subtype of a listed type.
If \VAR{T} has static parameters,
these statements hold of each instantiation of \VAR{T},
with the static parameters of \VAR{T} in the listed types
replaced by the corresponding static arguments.
\revision{revival-comprises}{The Working Draft of February 2011 said here,
in a draft note, that the traits listed in a \KWD{comprises} clause
are exactly the traits that immediately extend \VAR{T}
and that each of them must list \VAR{T} in its \KWD{extends} clause.
The revival states the reading of the team's later Types chapter
(Luchangco, 2012) and of the type group's calculus Welterweight Fortress (2012):
the clause says to which types the values of \VAR{T} belong.
A parameterized trait with a static parameter that \VAR{T} does not have
can be listed only at particular static arguments;
it may stand unlisted between \VAR{T} and the listed types,
adding no value outside them,
when at least one trait or object extends it
and every one that does is a subtype of a listed type.
This also answers the third question of the draft note on trait identifiers above,
whether an instantiation of a parameterized trait may be listed: it may.
A \KWD{where}-clause variable of the declaration of \VAR{T} may also occur in a
listed type, as in the clause of the trait \TYP{NatParam} of \library,
which the team wrote as a comment and the revival restores.}
\note{
If the \KWD{comprises} clause of a trait \VAR{T} includes ``\EXP{\ldots}''
(and must therefore be in an API),
then in a component exporting the enclosing API,
other traits may explicitly extend \VAR{T},
but these traits may not be declared or imported by the API
(see \secref{apis}).}

== explorations/fortress-gap-ledger.md:7-27

## The row template

A row is one line of eight cells, `| # | claim | status | class | spec citation | reproducer | found by | notes / workaround |`, at most 1,200 characters, in the table of its topic section, in number order. A pipe inside a cell is written `\|`. (POSITIONS, "The gap ledger's form"; the proposal behind it is `explorations/coordinator/process-engineering/gap-ledger-archaeology.md`, section 4.)

- **#**: the row's number, the next free one when it is added; never reused, renumbered or given to another row. 148 is vacant.
- **claim**: at most 300 characters, whose first 150 name the defect or the capability: what fails or what holds, and where.
- **status**: exactly one word of seven, with no second status and nothing in brackets:
  - `POSITIVE-VERIFIED`: it works; it ran and its output is recorded.
  - `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`: the specification settles it and the reproducer confirms it. A row with one half fixed stays `NEGATIVE-VERIFIED`, and its notes say which half is fixed.
  - `NEGATIVE-BOUNDED`: the failure reproduces; the mechanisms tried are named and are not exhaustive.
  - `CONTESTED`: unsettled; the notes say why.
  - `RETIRED`: a source's claim falsified here, kept so that it is not derived again.
  - `FIXED`: closed by a landed commit (`ledger.py close`): the claim's first sentence, the test as reproducer, notes `fixed HASH; full text: history, row N`.
  - `DUPLICATE`: a pointer (`ledger.py duplicate`), notes `duplicate of row M; full text: history, row N`.
- **class**: `kind (area)`; `—` only for `POSITIVE-VERIFIED` and `RETIRED`. The kind is one of `implementation gap`, `library gap vs spec`, `library bug`, `design limit`, `deliberate`, `typesetter`, `packaging`; the area one of `parser`, `walk`, `checker`, `codegen`, `runtime`, `library`, `prelude`, `specification`, `tests`, `tools`.
- **spec citation**: the `.tex` file and the section heading in quotes, as `basic/operators/juxtameaning.tex`, "Juxtaposition"; a line number only against `Specification-1.0-frozen/`; `silent` where the specification does not say.
- **reproducer**: one test (its name, or its path under the test folders; an `XXX` test while it is an expected failure) or one probe path from the repository root, at most 200 characters; `none` when nothing in the tree reproduces it, with the command and its output, or the probe's old path, in the notes.
- **found by**: the stream that found it (`climb batch 8 rung I`, `run-c3`, `apl rung 2`), at most 60 characters; no date and no role.
- **notes / workaround**: at most 700 characters: `siblings: N, M` first if there are any; the mechanism, with file:line and the commit it was true at; the workaround; for a closed row, `fixed HASH`.

A path under `explorations/` that is no longer in the tree is read from history: `git show $(git log -1 --diff-filter=D --format=%h -- PATH)^:PATH`.

content.content:
An \KWD{extends} clause comes first, if any, and
\KWD{excludes},
\KWD{comprises},
and \KWD{where}
clauses come in any order.

Each of \KWD{extends}, \KWD{excludes}, and \KWD{comprises} clauses consists
of \KWD{extends}, \KWD{excludes}, and \KWD{comprises}
respectively followed by a set of trait references
separated by commas and enclosed in braces `\txt{\{}' and `\txt{\}}'.
If such a clause contains only one trait, the enclosing braces may be elided.
In an API (but not a component),
a \KWD{comprises} clause may include ``\EXP{\ldots}''.
A trait reference listed in the \KWD{comprises} clause is a declared
trait identifier (within the same component or an API imported by the
component).
\note{
Victor: Why is this property stated only for a comprises clause?
Doesn't it apply to extends and excludes clauses as well?
Also, do we really mean ``trait identifier'' above?  Where is that
term defined?  Does it include instantiations of parametric traits?}

A trait with an \KWD{extends} clause
\emph{explicitly extends} those traits listed in its \KWD{extends} clause.
\note{
Victor: It is possible for a trait to explicitly extend itself
 using hidden type variables.  In particular, the straightforward
 interpretation of covariant/contravariant declarations has this property.
 (But we could just rule this a special case, since it is special in other
 ways already.)
}
\revision{revival-where}{The revival rules on this note and on the
one below: a \KWD{where}-clause variable may not appear as a static
argument in an \KWD{extends} clause (\secref{where-clauses}),
so no trait extends itself through a hidden type variable
and explicit extension has no self cycles.}
In addition, every trait except \TYP{Any} and \TYP{Object}
implicitly extends the trait \TYP{Object}
if it does not do so explicitly.
We define the extension relation to be the transitive closure
of implicit and
explicit extension.
That is, trait \VAR{T} \emph{extends} trait \VAR{U}
if and only if \VAR{T} explicitly or implicitly
extends \VAR{U} or if there is some trait \VAR{S}
that \VAR{T} explicitly extends and that extends \VAR{U}.
The extension relation induced by a program is the smallest
relation satisfying these conditions.
This relation must form an acyclic hierarchy
rooted at trait \TYP{Object}.

# Rung S, climb batch 14: the skeptic's verdict

Verdict: **approved**, with one fix of the change and four corrections, none contested.

- Head judged: `20193383e`, the worker's last commit. The worker's REPORT.md and record.md were written onto the branch from the run's journal (`journal-text.py`, both writes exit 0) and committed alone at `dfbe11194`.
- My commits: `9a2cc93af`, `207eb7f06`, `63e507ba4` (corrections), `37f02419d` (the fix, "Skeptic's fix:"), `302aee6d6` (correction), then this file.
- The report's count and distance tables are those of the worker's head (`7612a9477`'s code). I ran no stage after my fix: the gate's tables on the merged tree are the record. By reading, my fix changes nothing the stages read (below, F1).

## 1. What I checked, and what it rests on

1. **The tables, against the worker's files.** `tmp/rung-self-type/distance-postedit.txt` holds "#total 55", "#seconds 1552 FortressLibrary 847"; `explorations/coordinator/tools/distance/compare.sh explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-13b/gate/distance.txt tmp/rung-self-type/distance-postedit.txt` prints "DISTANCE DOWN 85 -> 55 (-30)", "class S1 29 -> 0 (-29)", "class R4 1 -> 0 (-1)", "class BR 4 -> 3 (-1)", "class OT 16 -> 17 (+1)". `tmp/rung-self-type/checker-count-postedit.txt` holds "#total 1", and its diff against `climb-batch-13b/gate/checker-count.txt` is empty. My own comparison of the run's `errors.tsv` with `explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv`, matched by location and message (a short Python script over the two files), lists 31 rows gone and 1 come. Gone: the 29 (per-site rows 16, 17, 20-27, 31, 34, 36-39, 54-60, 70-75), row 76 (`FortressLibrary.fss:130`, BR, row 488's site) and row 78 (`:688`). Come: `:688` only, as "Right-hand side has type (Integral[\I\] & {I}), but declared type is ZZ.". This agrees with the report's section 4.
2. **Test first, in the worker's transcript** (`agent-a07c4afccdaa490de.jsonl`). It wrote the nine tests at 00:59:37-01:00:00. Its harness run on the base's code, call `fHPJnY`, ran 01:00:07-01:00:13Z and ended "Tests run: 9,  Failures: 9,  Errors: 0", with the lines recordedFailure quotes. After that run it applied the judgement's patch (`git apply`, call `nrHLq1`, 01:00:30). It then wrote the code: `UF6nxz` at 01:03:38 and `socpeZ` at 01:04:34 (python writes), and `MHfPj1` at 01:03:53 (`sed -i` on `Disambiguator.java`). The first build, `3vw2iL`, started at 01:04:49 and printed "BUILD SUCCESSFUL". The tests passed at 01:07:43 (`vWcyBc`, "OK (9 tests)"). The last run after its last change of code is `ant testQuick` at 01:42:45 (`SdAW9d`): `TEST-RESULTS/fast-compiler` "Tests run: 1127, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0", "BUILD SUCCESSFUL". The first `XXX` test was shown red on a deliberate fix at 01:08:01 (`awRih4`: "Saw wrong failure. compile"). The order holds.
3. **The diff against the section, the specification and the decisions.**
   - `FunctionalMethod.java` is the judgement's patch byte for byte: the diff's index line `1efa6cd45..ae6dad884` is the patch's (`explorations/reviews/self-typed-bodies-judgement.md`, "The patch").
   - `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala` holds the patch's rule (a), the coordinator's widened reading (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-14.md:86`, `:118`) and an own-name test that also accepts an api-qualified name. That test is harmless, since both names must print alike.
   - `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala` holds rule (b) as two functions of their own. `checkDeclComprises` and `checkObjectExprComprises` are untouched.
   - The specification passages are where the section puts them.
   - Two places in the text said less than the checker does (F2). One place in the code read a raw trait of another api in the wrong scope (F1).
4. **Where the fix belongs, and the precedents.** The team's own self type under a `comprises` clause is in the disambiguator, and rule (a) reuses it. `checkObjectExprComprises` is the precedent for the object-expression walk. Name resolution follows `TypeDisambiguator.handleTypeName`. No device was invented where the tree has one.
5. **The tests.** Each test file has one comment line and is named by its topic, with no citation in a message. Each one exercises its rule: the base's run shows the sites' own message, "Function body has type Shape[\S\], but declared return type is S.".
6. **My own programs**, under `tmp/rung-self-type/skeptic/` (section 3).
7. **The three homes** (section 4).
8. **The ledger and sibling sites.**
   - `ledger-find` with my own words ("self type", "self-typed", "F-bound*", "Containment*", "extends Equality", "object expression*", the two class names) finds rows 695, 407, 488, 355, 375, 414 and 570. Row 414 (the declaration rule at a static parameter) and row 570 (object expressions in the overloading check) are not moved.
   - For siblings, my scan of every `.fss` and `.fsi` in the tree (`tmp/rung-self-type/skeptic/extenders.py`) lists every declaration that extends one of the 16 self-typed traits of `Library/` at a type other than its own name. Only the trips demo's `generator` extends one at another type (`ProjectFortress/demos/trips.fss:96`). The rest extend at a type parameter: the library's chains, PureList's `List[\E\]` (`Library/PureList.fsi:41`), the two `Containment` mixins, and the team's test copies, `Compiled17ee`, `other_compiler_tests/Gen0.fss` and `not_working_library_tests/MatchErrorBug.fss`. Each of those is bounded by its own trait except `List` and the two mixins.
   - The compiler's prelude declares no F-bound without a clause: `Library/CompilerAlgebra.fsi:16`, `:24` use `comprises T`. So rule (a) changes no prelude body that the code generator compiles.
   - On the other path there is nothing to change: walk reads a self type by its named trait alone (`interpreter/evaluator/EvalType.java:51-53`, `:535-537`).
9. **The report.**
   - I opened each provenance line with `sed -n`. Each says what its line holds: `climb-batch-13b/gate/distance.txt:16-17` holds the S1 and R4 classes, `var-ref.tex:53-54` the self sentence, `SelfParamDisambiguator.scala:68-69` at the base the clause case, `TypeHierarchyChecker.scala:66-100` at the base `checkObjectExprComprises`, `traits.tex:285-286` the new term, and `changes.tex:3296` the entry.
   - The worker's whole-suite runs are on `7612a9477`'s code, with the verdicts the report quotes.
   - The worker lists every point to report that the rung reaches.
   - record.md is true as written, but for row 695's bound and the clause wording that I corrected (F3).
10. **Competing declarations.** None of the rung's 9 test components and none of my 4 new test components or 4 apis has a name that occurs elsewhere in the test corpora. The same holds for the new Scala and Java names: `selfParamPosition`, `checkDeclSelfParams`, `checkObjectExprSelfParams`, `selfParamArg`, `selfIndexOf`, `throughBound`, `resolveTrait`, `homeOf` and `selfFromBound` each occur only in the files that declare and call them. The sibling branches' new test files have other names (`git diff --name-only` of `origin/wip/rung-argument-context` and `origin/wip/rung-popl-examples`).
11. **The failure-mode question.** The rung turns a loud refusal into acceptance and a value. Under rule (a), a body that returns `self` as the self-type parameter now compiles. At run time it answers the receiver when the parameter is a trait type (`SkSelfSuperType`, "cat"). It dies loudly with `VerifyError: Bad return type` when the parameter is an object type (row 695).
